# Button

Button: triggers an action.

Also asked as: cta, submit.

**Import:** `import { Button } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Button/Button.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Button/Button.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Spacing, Icons, States, Default, Primary, Subtle, Warning, Danger, Discovery, Ai, Compact, Selected, Disabled, Loading, FitContainer, Truncation, Interactive, StateSteps, KeyboardFocus, AnchorKeyboard, AnchorHref

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Button/Button.mdx`

## Usage

Use a button for an action on the current page: submit a form, mark attendance, close a dialog. For navigation to another page, use Link button.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Most actions that are not the main call to action of a page or area. Less prominent than primary. Example: "Reschedule session". |
| Primary | The main call to action or a form submission. One per page or area. Example: "Book session". |
| Subtle | Secondary actions next to a primary button, and places where it is already clear items are interactive, such as toolbars and button groups. Example: "Cancel" beside "Save notes". |
| Warning | Confirms an action that may cause a significant change or a loss of data, often in a confirmation modal. Example: "Remove from this week". |
| Danger | The final confirmation of a destructive, irreversible action such as deleting. Example: "Delete session recording". |
| Discovery | The call to action for a new experience. Example: "Try the new schedule view". |
| AI | The one primary AI action in a region. Draws the sparkle before its label. Example: "Generate summary". |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use sentence case: "Add student". | Title case or all capitals: "Add Student", "ADD STUDENT". |
| Keep the label short and free of punctuation: "Save notes". | "Save the notes for this session." |
| Start with a verb and name what is acted on: "Confirm session time". | Vague labels such as "OK", "Yes" or "Submit". |
| Use the same words as the heading and related text in view. | Different words for the same action within one view. |

## Best practices

### One primary action per area. {#one-primary-action-per-area}

Do: One primary button, with the secondary action subtle beside it.
Don't: Two primary buttons in one area compete for attention.

### One primary AI action per region. {#one-primary-ai-action-per-region}

The AI appearance marks the single main AI action in a region, such as "Generate summary" on a session's notes. Use it only for actions that call AI, never to emphasize an ordinary action, and leave its look as shipped: no custom color, icon or fill (the sparkle is always drawn and a label is required). Every other AI action in the region is a default or subtle button with an AI icon.

Do: One AI button for the region's main AI action, with the other actions subtle.
Don't: A second AI button competes with the first, and Save notes is not an AI action.

### Pick the spacing for the surrounding space. {#pick-the-spacing-for-the-surrounding-space}

Default spacing for most places; compact for tables and tight spaces, such as a row of student sessions.

### Keep a form's submit button pressable. {#keep-a-form-s-submit-button-pressable}

Do: Explain what is missing with validation text under the field.
Don't: A disabled submit button gives no direction and leaves the tab order.

### Align the primary button with its group. {#align-the-primary-button-with-its-group}

Right-align buttons in focused tasks and modal dialogs, with the primary on the right. Left-align on single-page forms and full-page tasks with a lot of content, with the primary on the left.

## Accessibility

- A button performs an action; a link navigates. Use the right element so screen readers announce the right role.
- Avoid `isDisabled`. A disabled button leaves the tab order and receives no events. Use validation and on-screen directions instead, and never attach a tooltip to one.
- A button with no visible label is an Icon button, which requires a `label`.
- Loading blocks interaction and sets `aria-busy`; the label stays in the tree for assistive technology.
- Selected is not color alone: `isSelected` sets `aria-pressed`.
- The focus ring is 2px in `--ds-border-focused`. Never remove it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string | — | The label. Children work too. |
| `children` | node | — | The label, used when `text` is not given. Omit both for an icon-only button. |
| `title` | string | — | The `title` attribute, a native tooltip on hover. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | The visual style. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | Height and padding: `default` draws 32, `compact` draws 24. Compact is for tables and tight toolbars. |
| `shouldFitContainer` | bool | `false` | Stretches the button to the width of its container. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the button element beside the component's own. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event when the button is activated by mouse or keyboard. It does not fire while `isDisabled` or `isLoading` is set. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Prevents interaction. Avoid it; see Usage. |
| `isSelected` | bool | — | Marks the button selected and sets `aria-pressed`. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | Shows a spinner in place of the label and blocks interaction. |
| `type` | string | `'button'` | The native button `type`: `button` (default), `submit` or `reset`. Used only when the button renders as a `button` element. |
| `as` | elementType | — | Renders the button as this element or component instead, such as a router link. Without it the button is an anchor when `href`, `target` or `rel` is set, otherwise a `button`. |
| `href` | string | — | Renders as an anchor when set (and no `as` overrides it). |
| `target` | string | — | The anchor `target` attribute, such as `_blank`. Used only when the button renders as an anchor. |
| `rel` | string | — | The anchor `rel` attribute. Used only when the button renders as an anchor. |
| `role` | string | — | Overrides the default `"button"` ARIA role an anchor-rendered Button takes (e.g. `LinkButton`'s own `"link"`). |
| `iconBefore` | string or node | — | A Font Awesome Free glyph name, or a node, before the label. |
| `iconAfter` | string or node | — | A Font Awesome Free glyph name, or a node, after the label. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the rendered element. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Related

- To act with an icon alone, use Icon button.
- To navigate in the look of text, use Link button.
- For a set of choices the user picks between, use `RadioGroup`.
- For a menu of actions behind one trigger, use `DropdownMenu`.
- To show that work is under way on the page rather than in the control, use `ProgressBar`.
